'''Gerald Gendall Fuller''' (born April 7, 1953) is a Canadian/American [[chemical engineer]] and [[Fletcher Jones (American entrepreneur)|Fletcher Jones]] II Professor of [[Chemical Engineering]] at [[Stanford University]]. He received his B.S. in chemical engineering from the [[University of Calgary]] in 1975 and his PhD in [[chemical engineering]] from [[Caltech]] in 1980.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://cpima.stanford.edu/cpima/fuller/ |title=CPIMA » CPIMA Participants » Fuller |access-date=2009-09-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090509004928/http://cpima.stanford.edu/cpima/fuller/ |archive-date=2009-05-09 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Fuller participates in Stanford's CPIMA, a joint venture between the [[University of California]] and [[IBM]], and is known for his work on the [[rheology]] of complex fluid interfaces and biocompatible structures, which has applications in [[tissue engineering]]. He authored a textbook on the optical rheometry of complex fluids.

In 2005, Fuller was elected as a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] for contributions toward understanding the rheology of [[complex fluid]]s, fluid interfaces and rheo-optical technique development.
